# Script to run "Gblocks". This will clean the alignments, removing gap-rich regions. Important to use the codon-aware flag (-t=c) so that the reading frame doesnt get disrupted.

```{bash, eval=FALSE}
#!/bin/bash -l
#SBATCH -J gBlocks
#SBATCH --mail-type FAIL,DONE
#SBATCH --mail-user Julia.Levinstein@campus.lmu.de
#SBATCH -t 2-00:00:00
#SBATCH --clusters=biohpc_gen
#SBATCH --partition=biohpc_gen_normal
#SBATCH --mem=4G
#SBATCH -n 1
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=1
#SBATCH --output=gblocks.out



eval "$(conda shell.bash hook)"
CONDA_ENV_PATH="/dss/dsslegfs01/pr53da/pr53da-dss-0036/projects/2025__neosex/conda_envs/bio_env"
conda activate "$CONDA_ENV_PATH"

WORK_DIR="/dss/dsslegfs01/pr53da/pr53da-dss-0036/projects/2025__neosex/neosex_project/fusion_dating"
CLADE="Meliphagidae"
GENES="autosomal_genes"


TARGET_DIR="$WORK_DIR/$CLADE/$GENES/PAML_constraint_str"


if [ ! -d "$TARGET_DIR" ]; then
    echo "Error: Directory $TARGET_DIR does not exist."
    exit 1
fi

echo "Starting Gblocks run across subdirectories in $TARGET_DIR..."

find "$TARGET_DIR" -type f -name "*_NT.fasta" | while read -r alignment_file; do
    echo "Processing: $alignment_file"

    # Run Gblocks
    # Common flags:
    #   -t=d (DNA) or -t=p (Protein) or -t=c (Codons)
    # important to keep it codon-aware for PAML analysis
    #   -b5=h (Allowed gap positions: n=none, h=half, a=all)
    Gblocks "$alignment_file" -t=c -b5=h

done


```
